note: Entries are [year, TWh, population, peak_factor] for the 50 states and DC, keyed by ISO 3166-2 code, derived by scripts/derive-subnational-demand.py. 6 of the 51 have a peak factor; peak_basis gives, for each, its BAs, their share of the state's retail sales, the hours used, and the mean, peak and peak hour of their hourly sum.

method.twh: Annual retail sales to ultimate customers, all sectors (TOTAL Sales, MWh), summed over Parts A, B and D as the file's footnote prescribes for state totals; this includes the "Adjustment 2025" rows that stand for short-form (EIA-861S) respondents. Retail sales exclude direct use: electricity generated and used on site (industrial and commercial self-generation, customer-owned rooftop solar) is not in them, and neither are transmission and distribution losses. Third-party-owned behind-the-meter solar sold to the host customer is included (11.837 TWh nationally).
method.population: Census Bureau Vintage 2025 estimate of the resident population on 1 July 2025.
method.peak_factor: Annual peak hourly demand over mean hourly demand, from EIA-930 Demand (MW) (Adjusted) (EIA's series with anomalous and missing reports replaced by imputed values). A BA is in a state when at least 80% of its EIA-861 retail sales (by BA Code) lie in that state. When a state's in-state BAs that report at least 95% of the year's hours carry at least 80% of its sales, the factor is the maximum of their hourly sum over its mean, taken over the UTC hours every one of them reports; otherwise it is null and the generator uses its default. Hours that are not physically plausible are dropped per BA before summing: non-positive values and values above twice the BA's nearest-rank 99.9th percentile (hours dropped in the BAs used: FMPP 2, IID 122, NEVP 17, NYIS 2, SEC 2, TIDC 25). The factor is a ratio of BA demand, which includes losses and is net of behind-the-meter generation, applied to retail sales.
